fixes.explanation: Good memory, because Moses, Israel's leader, really did make a bronze serpent (Numbers 21:9). But this passage doesn't bring it up at all. Solomon gathers the leaders to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD (1 Kings 8:1). Right story, different shiny object.

Goliath, the giant David defeated, had a sword that people remember (1 Samuel 17:51). It isn't what Solomon's leaders gather for, though. The text says they're there to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Zion (1 Kings 8:1). I'd have loved to see a giant's sword carried up the street, but that's a different day.

Seven is a big number in the Bible, so I get the guess. But this verse doesn't say seven. It says the sheep and oxen were so many that they could not be counted or numbered (1 Kings 8:5). Seven of each is fourteen animals, and nobody loses count of fourteen.

I see the picture you had in mind. But the text doesn't say the wings lift anything. It says the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark and overshadow the ark and its poles (1 Kings 8:7). The ark stays where the priests set it.

Good try, friend, but the text gives the wings a different job. The cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark and overshadow the ark and its poles (1 Kings 8:7). They're spread out over the ark, and the text says nothing about the doors.

Manna is the food God provided for Israel in the wilderness (Exodus 16:4, 35), so I see why it came to mind. But this verse closes the door on extras. It says there was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets (1 Kings 8:9). No jar of manna is in the count.
Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), is an easy name to land on. But the text names someone else here. It says Moses had placed the tablets in the ark at Horeb (1 Kings 8:9). Moses is the one.

Joshua, Moses' attendant (Exodus 24:13), is a name that goes with Moses, so I understand the pick. But the text doesn't name him here. It says the two stone tablets were the ones Moses had placed in the ark at Horeb (1 Kings 8:9). Moses did the placing.

Yes. The text says the priests could not stand there to minister because of the cloud (1 Kings 8:11). Then it says, "For the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD." (1 Kings 8:11). The blank is glory.

I understand the guess, because the priests could not stand there to minister. But the text doesn't mention fear here. It says, "For the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD." (1 Kings 8:11). I'd only be guessing about how they felt, and the text gives us glory.

That's it. Solomon says to the LORD, "I have indeed built You an exalted house, a place for You to dwell forever." (1 Kings 8:13). He says it right after the cloud fills the house. Forever is the word he uses, friend.

I see why you'd say that, since the elders are named right at the start of the passage (1 Kings 8:1). But the text says Solomon blesses everybody. With the whole assembly of Israel standing there, the king turned around and blessed them all (1 Kings 8:14). Nobody gets left out of that blessing.

I understand the doubt, but the statement on this card matches the text. Solomon quotes God as saying that since the day He brought Israel out of Egypt, He had not chosen a city from any tribe of Israel to build a house so that His Name would be there (1 Kings 8:16). So the card is true. In the same verse God says, "But I have chosen David to be over My people Israel." (1 Kings 8:16).

Saul, made king at Gilgal (1 Samuel 11:15), is a name people reach for, so I understand the guess. But the verse names someone else. God says, "But I have chosen David to be over My people Israel." (1 Kings 8:16).

Kings are a reasonable guess with a king speaking. But Solomon says something else. He says the covenant was made with "…our fathers when He brought them out of the land of Egypt." (1 Kings 8:21). The fathers are the ones he names, friend.
